name: Yiqing Wang

papers.title: Being-H0.5: Scaling Human-Centric Robot Learning for Cross-Embodiment Generalization
papers.abstract: We present Being-H0.5, a Vision-Language-Action foundation model for cross-embodiment generalization. To address morphological diversity and data scarcity, we propose a human-centric learning paradigm treating human interaction traces as a universal ``mother tongue'' for physical skills. We curate a 35,000-hour embodied pre-training corpus spanning human and 30 robotic embodiments. Central to our approach is a unified action space that maps human hand motion and heterogeneous robot controls into semantically aligned slots, enabling low-resource robots to bootstrap from human and high-resource platforms. Built on this foundation, we develop unified sequence modeling and multi-task pre-training to jointly learn from human demonstrations and robot trajectories. Architecturally, Being-H0.5 extends conventional Mixture-of-Transformers with a novel Mixture-of-Flow, which separates shared motor primitives from embodiment-specific action experts. For real-world stability, we introduce Manifold-Preserving Gating to mitigate sensory shift and Universal Async Chunking for chunked control across varying latencies and control rates. Being-H0.5 achieves state-of-the-art results on LIBERO and RoboCasa, and demonstrates strong cross-embodiment performance across five real robot platforms.
topics: 视觉语言动作与基础模型
